items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: In that original reed section... The tenor players were named Lucky... Warren Lucky was one of the tenor player's names... I was playing the lead and most of the solos.

ctx.x: and he was giving me some fatherly advice, you know. And anyway, I joined the band, Ernie Fields' band. And we got to Pensacola, Florida; we played a dance in Pensacola. Our next stop was Monroe, Louisiana. [LAUGHS] Our next stop was Tulsa, Oklahoma! I'm gettin' farther and farther' away from New York, right...! [LAUGHS] So I stayed out there with them, and I began to get attached to the guys, you know, and be like a part of the band, and so you get sentimental, you know... So I ended up staying there with him.

And he had a very, very fine vocalist with this band, Melvin Moore. Great singer. Sing anything. In fact, he was really carrying the band until I got there and helped him carry it. Because when I went, I was playing the lead and most of the solos. In that original reed section, they had John White on one alto, and had... The baritone player was named Sy. And the tenor players were named Lucky... Warren Lucky was one of the tenor player's names; he was from Dallas, Texas -- good saxophone player. And the other…
